onboarding.title: A clear start with your money
onboarding.intro: Prospera helps you turn everyday money choices into a plan you can trust. Start simple, build a little history, then set a budget that reflects real life.

steps.title: Your first three steps
steps.envelopes: Create at least one revenue envelope and three expense envelopes. Begin with broad categories such as Paycheck, Housing, Groceries and Transport.
steps.ledger: Create a ledger to record income and spending. Add one transaction for each envelope and keep recording for 30 days.
steps.budget: After 30 days of history, create your first draft budget. Prospera starts it with each envelope's net activity from the last 30 days; adjust the plan before publishing.

envelopes.title: Create and manage envelopes
envelopes.summary: Set up simple categories for money coming in and going out.
envelopes.body:
Envelopes give each part of your money a purpose. Start with a small set: Paycheck for income, then Housing, Groceries, Transport, Utilities and Savings for expenses.

Keep categories broad at first. You can add more detail when your records show that it would help. Give each envelope a clear name and choose whether it represents revenue or expense.

Use the Envelopes page to add, rename, recolor or share envelopes. Each envelope keeps its direction once it is used in a budget or transaction.

ledgers.title: Create and manage ledgers
ledgers.summary: Choose a starting balance and a clear period for recording what happens.
ledgers.body:
A ledger is the record of money that actually came in or went out. Its starting balance is your cash or debt at the beginning of the period. Choose an opening date and a closing date that fit your plan.

Ledgers use whole calendar months. Many people use a 12-month period; shorter periods can work too. Keep ledger periods consistent so it is easier to compare what you planned with what happened.

At the closing date, review the result. A balanced period is useful; a positive net result gives you more room for the next goal. Close a ledger when its period is finished, then create the next one.

transactions.title: Create and manage transactions
transactions.summary: Record each real payment or deposit against the envelope it belongs to.
transactions.body:
A transaction is one real movement of money. Add the date, choose its envelope and enter the positive amount; Prospera uses the envelope's direction to record it as revenue or expense.

Record transactions regularly, including deposits and everyday purchases. A steady record helps you spot habits, follow payments and understand where money comes from and goes.

Transactions belong to a ledger, but do not require a budget. You can correct an entry by deleting it and recording the right one.

budgets.title: Create and manage budgets
budgets.summary: Turn your transaction history into a monthly plan, then adjust it as life changes.
budgets.body:
A budget is a goal for one month: expected income and the amounts you plan for each expense envelope. The first draft uses each envelope's net transactions from the trailing 30 days as a starting point—not a promise or a limit. Review and adjust every amount.

A draft can be changed as often as you need. When it reflects your plan, publish it for the current month. Published budgets are read-only; create a revision if your plan changes.

The Budget page compares your plan with recorded spending. Use it to make deliberate adjustments, not to judge yourself for an unexpected bill.

progress.title: Your setup progress
progress.envelopes: Still needed: {revenue} revenue envelope(s) and {expenses} expense envelope(s).
progress.budget: For your first budget: {days} more day(s) of history and transactions in {envelopes} more envelope(s).

onboarding.encouragement: Small, regular steps add up. You are building a clearer picture—not chasing perfection.
